messages:
Sam (Sales): Heads up - WaveCorp is evaluating swapping vendors. They want a 5-day tech POC focusing on API parity, edge-case responses, and a pricing runbook. They also asked about on-prem footprint and SSO. Can we mobilize?
Ana (Solutions): Yes. Recommend we offer: 1) API adapter (drop-in endpoints) 2) golden corpus run (200 prompts) 3) drift report (behavioral + token delta) 4) cost projection. Need their example traffic and current model IDs.
Customer-CTO: They will provide sample logs (anonymized) and 20 'must-match' prompts. Must not persist PII. Also want a fallback strategy during cutover.
Leo (SE): We can spin an adapter that exposes their existing endpoints and translates to Redwood's API. Two things to flag: streaming chunk boundaries and function-calling semantics differ. We should force non-streaming deterministic responses for parity tests.
Ravi (Eng): Agree. We'll run tokenizer parity and a deterministic decode. For streaming parity tests use a chunk-normalizer shim. Small formatting diffs (commas, bullet markers) will be common; shim can normalize whitespace and punctuation.
Sam (Sales): Timeline: customer demo Fri. Can Solutions + Eng produce a one-page plan today?
Dana (Legal): Also note: their security team sent an NDA + SOC checklist. I'll prefill the SOC answers but need to confirm data residency for on-prem.
Pri (Finance): Pricing note: for POC we typically offer usage credits. If they move to dedicated, we give a transition credit applied to first 3 months. Need to know expected sustained qps to ballpark dedicated tier.
deploy-bot: Sandbox created: wavecorp-poc-1780. Credentials delivered to Ana via DM.
Ana (Solutions): Received creds. Customer-CTO: please upload the 20 must-match prompts and the sample traffic trace (last 7 days) to the sandbox.
Customer-CTO: Done. Uploaded prompts.csv and traffic.json (anonymized).
Leo (SE): Running compare job now. I'll use the following curl template for adapter test: ```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://sandbox.redwood.internal/v1/adapter/invoke \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"endpoint":"/generate","payload":{"input":"Summarize: \"text...\"","max_tokens":120},"compat_mode":"vendor-v1"}'
```
This sets compat_mode which applies deterministic seed + response-shape mapping.
Ravi (Eng): Also prepping a small compare tool that computes token_count_diff, BLEU-ish score, and a structural JSON diff. Will upload artifacts to the sandbox under /results/1780.
Leo (SE): Early results: 20 must-match items -> 18 exact intent + 2 minor structure mismatches (missing top-level field). We can shim those in the adapter quickly. Average token delta +3 tokens per request.
Ana (Solutions): Good. Add success criteria: >=95% intent parity for must-match prompts, structural mapping applied for mismatches, and <=15% projected cost increase.
Sam (Sales): Also include rollback policy: live traffic can be routed 5% to Redwood with automatic failover to legacy provider on >2% error spike.
Customer-CTO: Acceptable. Also ask: can you run with no remote prompt logs for my users? Compliance requires ephemeral-only retention.
Dana (Legal): We support ephemeral mode. We'll document it in the SOW and add required attestation language. For on-prem, we need network egress matrix to confirm offline install compatibility.
Pri (Finance): For dedicated pricing ballpark: small (dedicated vPool) ~$Yk/month, medium ~$Zk/month. I'll prepare a detailed tier table once Eng reports qps.
Ravi (Eng): Uploaded initial diffs and compare CSV to sandbox:/results/1780/diff_report.csv. Notable: streaming chunk order differs in 4/200 tests; shim normalizer fixes it. Latency median is 12% lower than their current provider in our sandbox bench.
Leo (SE): Adding a small runbook: "if unmatched structure -> apply response-mapping v0.1 -> re-run golden tests -> enable canary at 1% traffic". I'll attach to SOW.
Sam (Sales): Great. Dana, can Legal share a redline NDA + SAML exchange template?
Dana (Legal): Sharing NDA + SAML template links via DM. Also ping me if their security team requests encryption-at-rest details.
deploy-bot: Canary route configured: 1% traffic -> redwood-adapter-1780. Monitoring hooks enabled.
Customer-CTO: We'll join the canary review tomorrow. One final ask: can you provide an itemized run-rate calc showing tokenization mapping assumptions?
Ana (Solutions): Yes. We'll produce run-rate spreadsheet with two columns: their token accounting vs our token accounting (post-mapping) and estimated monthly cost at current QPS. Deliverable by EOD tomorrow.
Sam (Sales): Thanks team. Keeping this thread open for artifacts + SOW finalization.
Pri (Finance): I'll standby to finalize numbers once we get the qps from Eng.
Ravi (Eng): Final note: behavior drift largely around list rendering and currency formatting. Adapter will normalize locale-specific formats. Uploading fix now.
Ana (Solutions): Closing action list: SOW draft, risk register, run-rate calc, adapter code, and compare artifacts. Aiming to share before demo on Fri.
